Election Commission of India (ECI)
Articles 324-329 (Part XV) • Formed on 26 Jan, 1950.

Administers the election to es ors photo identity the LS, RS, LA, LC, President, cards started in 1993.

Composition: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + 2 Election Commissioners (as determined by the President)
Appointment: By President.
Tenure: 6 years or until 65 years of age
Election Commissioner cannot be Re-appointed in same office.
Removal: By President, Similar to the removal procedure of a Supreme Court Judge (CEC), other ECs are removed by President on the advice of CEC.
Salary: Same as a Supreme Court Judge
Nature of functions: Administrative, Advisory, Quasi- judicial.
1st CEC: Sukumar Sen
Current Election Commissioner - Gyanesh Kumar (26th).
Originally it was a single-membered body.
It became a Multi-membered body for the 1st time in 1989, permanently from 1st Oct 1993.
61st Amendment of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.
Important Articles:
Article 324; Superintendence, direction and control of elections.
_• 19th CA, 1966, Amended article 324 of the Indian constitution to abolish the system of Election Tribunals for resolving election disputes.
Article 325: No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
Article 326: Elections on the basis of adult suffrage, Representation of People Act.
Article 327: Powers of Parliament to make provisions with respect to elections to legislature.
Article 328: Power of Legislature of a State to make provi- sions with respect to elections to such legislature.
Article 329: Prohibits interference by courts in electoral matters.
Chapter 1 - Services (Article 308-314)
Article 308: Defines the term "State" for Part XIV and serves as an interpretative provision governing services under the Union and the States.
Article 309: Recruitment and conditions of service of per- sons serving the Union or a State.
Article 310: Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State.
Article 311: Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in Civil capacities under the Union or a State.
Article 312: All India Services.
Article 312A: Added through 28th CA, 1972, Power of parliament to vary or revoke conditions of service of officers of certain services.
Article 313: Transitional provisions.
Article 314: Provision for protection of existing officers of certain services.
Chapter II - Public Service Commission (Articles 315- 323)
Independent Constitutional body; known as "Watchdog of Merit System"
Composition: in discretion of the President.
Qualification: 1/2 of members must have held Government office for 10 years.
Term: 6 years or until 65 years of age.
Do Recruitment: All India Services and Central Services.
Members Not Eligible for Employment other than as chairman of UPSC & SPSC once.
Removal by President if.
found insolvent (gone bankrupt).
found holding any office of profit.
having an infirmity of mind or body.
misbehaviour (as recommended by SC through an enquiry board).
Article 315: Public Service Commission for the Union and for the States.
Article 316: Appointment and term of office of members.
Article 317: Removal and suspension of a member of PSC.

Article 318: To make regulations as to conditions of service of members and staff of the Commission. pete Article 319: Prohibition as to the holding of office by members of commission on ceasing to be such members.
Article 320: Function of PSCs, Article 321: Power to extend functions of PSCs.
Article 322: Expenses of PSCs.
Article 323: Reports of PSCs.
State Public Service Commission (SPSC)
Articles 315-323 (Part XIV)
Same structure as UPSC
Term: 6 years or until 62 years of age (same for JPSC).
Qualification: 1/2 of members must have held Government office for 10 years
Recruitment: State Services
Appointed by: Governor of the State.
Removal: same as UPSC
Though UPSC and SPSC are constitutional bodies but Joint Public Service Commission is Statutory in nature.
Article 280: Defines Finance
Commission acts as the ex-officio
Secretary to the Council.
Composition: Chairman + 4 Members (Constituted by President in every 5 years.
Constitution has authorised Parliament to determine the Qualifications of member of Financial Commission.
Finance Commission is also known as Balancing wheel of Fiscal Federalism.
Qualifications:
Chairman - must be experienced in Public affairs.
Members - a judge of HC or Qualified to be appointed as a HC judge.
Special knowledge of finance and Accounts of government and Economics.
Experienced in Financial Matter and Administrations.
Members are eligible for reappointment.
Ist FC (1951): K C. Neogy
14th FC: Y.V. Reddy
15th FC: N.K. Singh
16th FC: Arvind Panagariya
Members: Ajay Narayan Jha, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh (Part-time)
Related Articles:
Article 281: Submission of recommendations of FC.

Inserted via 101st CAA, 2016
Article 279A:
Composition: Joint forum of Centre & State.
Chairperson: Union Finance Minister.
The GST council takes decisions by a 3/4th (75%) majority of weighted votes of members present and voting.
The Centre holds 1/3rd weightage, while the states together hold 2/3rd, ensuring cooperative federalism.
National Commission for SCs & STs
SCs - Article 338
STs - Article 338A
Tenure - 3 Years
Composition: Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + 3 members
All members appointed by President.
Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer for SCs and STs.
Later, the 65th CAA, 1990 replaced the Special Officer with a multimember National Commission for SCs and STs under Article 338.
Finally, the 89th CAA, 2003 bifurcated it into 2 separate commissions:
National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) — Article They have Power National Commission for Scheduled of Civil Courts.
Tribes (NCST) —Article 338A
National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)
Established in: 1993
Article: 338B:
Originally it was a statutory body.
Members 5 (Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, 3 Members appointed by President).
_• Mandal Case, 1992: SC directed Central government to constitute a permanent statutory body for Backward Class.
102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred the constitutional status and added a new article 338B to the constitution.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
Part V, Chapter V, Article 148-151
Head of the Indian Audit & Accounts Department
Term: 6 years or till 65 years of age K. Sanjay Murthy
Removal: Done in the same manner as that of SC Judge.
Known as: "Guardian of Public Purse"
B.R. Ambedkar mentioned CAG as the "Most important officer under the Constitution"
He acts as a Guide and Philosopher to Public Accounts Committee.
He compiles and maintains the accounts of State govern- ment, not central government.
CAG related Articles:
Article 148: Office of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), appointment, removal, salary and other conditions of service.
Article 149: Duties and powers of CAG.
Article 150: Form of accounts of the Union and of the States.
151(1) Audit reports must be submitted to President.
151(2) Reports related to the Account of the state shall be submitted to the Governor.
Article 279: CAG ascertains and certifies the Net Proceeds of any tax and that is final.
Attorney General of India Article 76: Highest Law Officer of India
Qualification: should be eligible to become a SC Judge.
Assisted by: Solicitor General (Not a constitutional body)
Advocate General of India Article 165: Appointed by: Governor
Qualification: must be eligible for a HC Judge
Advices State Government in legal matters referred to him by the Governor.
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
Established under Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 Composition:
Chairperson (Retired CJI or SC Judge) + 5 full-time members

Appointed by: President (based on 6-membered committee recommendation - PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman, Union Home Minister, Leader of Opposition Lok Sabha, Leader of Opposition Rajya Sabha.)
Tenure: 3 years or 70 years of age.
Members are eligible for re-appointment after completing their current term.
Also known as the "Watchdog of Human Rights"
Current Chairperson: Justice V. Ramasubramanian State Human Rights Commission
Chairperson (Retired Chief Justice or HC Judge) + 5 full- time members

Appointed by: Governor (based on 6-membered committee recommendation - CM, State home minister, Speaker of legislative assembly, Leader of opposition of (Assembly + Council), Chairperson of the legislative council).
Members are eligible for reappointment after completing their current term but not eligible for further employment under Centre or State.
Chief Information Commission (CIC)
Established in 2005 under Right to Information Act, 2005
Tenure: 5 years or 65 years of age
Not eligible for Reappointment under Central / State Government.
Appointment same as NHRC.
All constitutional authorities, including the President and the Supreme Court, all NGOs that are financed by the government come under the purview of RTI Act.
The Act mandates that the information be provided within 30 days of the request in normal cases.
Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)
Established: 1964 by Executive Resolution
Initial Status: Neither constitutional nor statutory.
Statutory Status granted in 2003
Tenure - 4 years / 65 years of age
Recommended by: Santhanam Committee
Appointed (on recommendation of 3 members committee - consisting of PM (as its head), Union Home Minister, Leader of opposition in L.S.)
3 Membered Body.
Established under Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
Lokpal term coined by - L.M. Singhvi in 1963.
—• Motto-Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption. This repla- ces the previous Motto - "Ma Gridhah Kasyasvidhanam" (Do not be greedy for anyone's wealth).
Equivalent to Ombudsman (Taken from Sweden).
Cannot take Suo-Motu action against Public Servants.
Preliminary Inquiries to be completed within 90 days.
Tenure - 5 Years / 70 years of age.
Maharashtra was the 1st State to establish the institution of Lokayukta in 1971.
Recommendations not binding on State Government.
Tenure - 5 Years / 65 years of age.
Composition:
Chairperson (Retd. CJI or SC Judge) + Maximum 8 Members 50% Judicial members + 50% from SC, ST, OBC, minorities, and women community.
1st Chairperson: Pinaki Chandra Ghose
Current Chairperson: Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar National Commission for Women
Established on 31st January 1992 under the provisions of NCW Act, 1990.
Current chairman - Vijaya Kishore Rahatkar (9th chairman).
University Grants Commission (UGC)

It is a statutory body established in 1956, operating under the Ministry of Education to coordinate, determine, and maintain standards of university education, teaching, examination, and research. Headquartered in New Delhi with six regional centers.
It provides funds to universities and advises governments on higher education improvement.
National Investigation Agency
NIA estd. in 2008 following mumbai terror attack under the NIA act, 2008.
Operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Headed by a Director General (DG).
The NIA investigates Terrorism, Nuclear and atomic offences, Hijacking, Smuggling of high-quality counterfeit Indian currency etc.
Can also investigate cases outside India if Central government directs it.
Special Courts (Sessions Courts) are established by the Central Government for trial of NIA cases.
Cases are tried in the Special Court where the offence was committed.
Transfer of Cases: Within states > High Court
Across states > Supreme Court
Appeals against Special Court judgments lie before the High Court EXECUTIVE BODIES Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
Established: 1963 by Executive Resolution
Derive its power from Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
It is an Executive body.
Law Commission of India
1st Law Commission (Pre-Independence): 1834, headed by Lord Macaulay e 1st Law Commission: 1955 (Post-Independence}
1st Law Commissioner: M.C. Setalvad (Post-Independence)
Function: Legal reform advisory
National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)
Formed on 1st Jan 2015 (replaced Planning Commission)
Governing Council: CMs of all States + Lt. Governors of UTs
Vice Chairman: Suman K Bery
Provides recommendations to the Government.
Serves as an advisory think tank to the government.
Governing Council of NITI Aayog consists of:- 1. Chief Minister of all states and UTs.
2. Lieutenant Governors of other UTs
Follows Bottom Up approach
Fosters Co-operative Federalism
NITI Aayog publishes: SDG India Index
National Multidimensional Poverty Index
